releaseScope.policy: Only deployed and pinned helpers become release evidence; helpers are not core launch contracts.

candidatePlan.note: Every predicted address, salt and configuration hash below is regenerated from source and is valid ONLY for the exact reviewed revision. Any source change re-mines all of them.
candidatePlan.nonceNote: The factory is deployed through the canonical CREATE2 proxy, so its address depends only on the proxy, factorySalt and init-code — never on the deployer nonce.
transactionOrder: Deploy ShardLaunchFactoryV1 through the CREATE2 proxy with factorySalt
postconditions: Deployed factory runtime matches the reviewed artifact and its immutable hookCreationCodeHash equals the value above
factory.renderer() equals expectedRenderer and the NFT is wired to the hook (nft.hook() == hook)
The hook address low 14 bits equal the five required v4 permission flags
The factory holds zero SHARD after launch and both liquidity positions are non-removable
candidatePlan.rendererSelection: address(0) at launch, resolving to the factory-deployed shared renderer above
candidatePlan.builderFeeRecipientNote: A compile-time constant on ShardLaunchFactoryV1, no longer a launch input. Rotatable after launch by the current builder via ShardFeeDistributorV1.setBuilderFeeRecipient.

factory.note: Runtime artifact is unpatched; deployment initcode adds 64 bytes of constructor arguments (poolManager, hookCreationCodeHash). The launcher recipient is a compile-time constant, not a constructor argument.

hookTemplate.note: Runtime artifact is unpatched; deployment initcode adds 288 bytes of constructor arguments. Its hash is recorded after launch inputs are fixed.

nftTemplate.note: Deployment initcode adds 64 bytes for the predicted hook and shared renderer. Its hash is recorded after launch inputs are fixed.

releaseBinding: releaseCommit is the git commit whose build every artifact size, hash and predicted address below was regenerated from. sourceCommitment is the git tree of src/ at that commit, so it identifies the reviewed contract bytes independently of documentation or manifest edits. A manifest cannot contain its own commit hash, so this binding is added in the commit that immediately follows the one it names; src/ is byte-identical across the two, which sourceCommitment is what proves.
